facts.quotation: User: Let's model a cooler, package CoolerStudy. The context has cooler of type Cooler and an external operator of type Operator.

facts.quotation: User: Probe sends TemperatureReading to Controller, then Controller sends CoolingCommand to Actuator. Name those ports readings and cooling respectively. Their channel types are Temperature and Cooling, with an output item at the sender and the conjugate type at the receiver. Use typed interfaces with directed flows.
facts.interpretation: TemperatureReading flows from probe.readings to controller.readings using Temperature sender and conjugate receiver.

facts.quotation: User: Probe sends TemperatureReading to Controller, then Controller sends CoolingCommand to Actuator. Name those ports readings and cooling respectively. Their channel types are Temperature and Cooling, with an output item at the sender and the conjugate type at the receiver. Use typed interfaces with directed flows.

facts.quotation: User: Operator outputs EnableCommand through enable, typed by an Enable channel. Cooler receives it through a conjugated enable boundary port. facts.interpretation: EnableCommand flows operator.enable to cooler.enable; cooler.enable binds controller.enable.
